multipleChoice.question: What question does the introduction raise about saunas?
options: Whether saunas should replace winter clothing.
Whether saunas offer real health benefits as well as warmth.
Whether saunas are cheaper in Britain than in Nordic countries.
Whether people should build saunas inside their homes.

multipleChoice.question: Why does James ask whether saunas are “all they’re cracked up to be”?
options: To argue that people should stop using them immediately.
To show that saunas are already medically proven.
To compare British saunas with Finnish bathhouses.
To question whether their reputation is fully deserved.

multipleChoice.question: What benefit does the first sauna user emphasise?
options: It helps them feel calm and comfortable.
It improves their ability to tolerate cold water.
It removes the need for regular exercise.
It helps them sleep for longer afterwards.

multipleChoice.question: According to the second user, when might a sauna be particularly useful?
options: When someone wants to avoid sweating.
When someone has no time to rest.
When someone’s muscles feel tight or tense.
When someone wants to train in high temperatures.

multipleChoice.question: How does the final sauna user describe the effect after being stressed?
options: It makes stress feel more serious than before.
It gives them a sense of starting afresh.
It distracts them without changing their mood.
It makes them dependent on daily sauna use.

multipleChoice.question: What is Professor Bailey’s general reaction to the research evidence?
options: He thinks it is too weak to discuss publicly.
He believes it only applies to professional athletes.
He is bored by the amount of evidence available.
He finds it impressive, although further testing is needed.

multipleChoice.question: Which figure is used to show how common sauna use is in Finland?
options: About 90% of the population use saunas.
About 40% of people use saunas every winter.
Thousands of people stopped using saunas.
Five million people took part in controlled trials.

multipleChoice.question: What limitation of the Finnish evidence is highlighted?
options: It ignores natural behaviour completely.
It was collected from only a few sauna-goers.
It is observational rather than fully controlled.
It proves that saunas cause every health improvement.

multipleChoice.question: Why does Damian say we should not “turn our noses up” at the current data?
options: Because controlled trials are impossible in any health research.
Because the evidence is large-scale even if it is not perfect.
Because Finnish culture should be copied without question.
Because observational data is always stronger than RCTs.

multipleChoice.question: What is the balanced conclusion about sauna evidence in the discussion?
options: It is promising and worth considering, but more controlled research would strengthen it.
It is useless because it has not yet been tested in a laboratory.
It proves that sauna use is the only reason Finnish people live longer.
It shows that personal relaxation benefits are unrelated to health outcomes.
